correctness.rationale: For nondegenerate homogeneous binary quadratic forms in even characteristic, the nonzero level meets each nonisotropic projective direction once, giving cardinality one less or one more than the field order. The alternating polar-form equation describes each prescribed nonzero pair sum. An isotropic sum is impossible; otherwise the conic intersection is governed by an Artin–Schreier quadratic, giving zero or two ordered representations. All diagonal pairs have sum zero. Character orthogonality gives the exact fourth-moment identity, and Cauchy–Schwarz and triangle inequalities give the optimal bound and equality iff the moduli are constant and the squared phases align. This includes the singleton conic. Rearrangement proves the exact two-term nonnegative deficit. The finite checker verifies 114 levels, 228 convolution identities, and eight direct Fourier normalizations; these tests do not replace the all-size proof.

Relevant published published-finding corpus findings were compared by objects, characteristics, and implications; the closest odd-characteristic conic theorem does not imply the binary-field case. value.rationale: The planar nondegenerate quadratic conic is a canonical finite-field restriction surface; its sharp endpoint and equality behavior in characteristic two are not given by the relevant odd-characteristic primary theorems. The result resolves the exact split/nonsplit constant for all even q, exhibits exponentially many discrete sign extremizers instead of merely constant functions, and supplies an exact amplitude-plus-squared-phase deficit. This is a natural complete endpoint classification and stability identity, not a numerical slice or an arbitrary parameter substitution. The restricted-Sidon mechanism explains its structural relation to finite harmonic analysis; historical equivalent formulations remain the principal value/originality risk.
